quotes.text: You typically have 10 calendar days from dispute creation to respond to a chargeback, and 6 calendar days to respond to an A-to-z Guarantee claim.
Amazon controls how long the customer has to complete this step; Stripe doesn't configure an authorization-session timeout.
Without expansion, `latest_charge` is a Charge ID.

old_evidence.text: You can create Amazon Pay payments in any of the supported currencies, regardless of the country your business operates in with the exception of the US.
You must submit the requested information within 10 calendar days.
For some Amazon Pay transactions that use non-card payment methods, refunds can take up to 14 calendar days from the purchase date to return a status.
After completing the payment, Amazon redirects them back to your website.

findings: Amazon Pay remains a reusable wallet using Amazon account credentials. New capture lists worldwide customers, AT/BE/CH/CY/DE/DK/ES/FR/GB/HU/IE/IT/LU/NL/PT/SE/US account locations, merchant or Connect platform, domestic/crossborder use, 12 presentment currencies for listed European locations and USD only for US, with 0.50 USD/GBP/EUR minima and linked other-currency minima. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:9-60; old raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md:8-12,16-22,56-76,136-151; current wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay.md:13-21.

New MCC 6051 crypto exchanges/wallets is prohibited; category eligibility is not proven merely by location/currency, and account-level availability still depends on enablement. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:18-30,190-194; current wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay.md:13-21 omits MCC restriction.

Manual and partial capture, recurring, full/partial refunds and full disputes remain supported, while extended/incremental auth and multi/over capture are not. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:62-87; old raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md:32-54. The new 90-day refund submission and up-to-14-calendar-day non-card final-status delay are distinct from refund succeeded; final refund.updated/refund.failed and failed-balance return are in raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:88-100 and old raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md:107-111.

The new dispute account separates chargebacks and A-to-z Guarantee claims: filing up to 240 calendar days for Amazon Pay disputes, 90 calendar days for A-to-z claims, usually 10 calendar days chargeback evidence but 6 for claims, authoritative deadline in Dispute.evidence_details.due_by, Amazon decision within 90 days after submission, disputed amount and applicable dispute fee withheld, winning amount/fee returned, and no fee for claims. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:102-143; old raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md:113-134; current wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay.md:23 presents a blanket 10-day evidence deadline.

New support matrix names Checkout full/embedded, Payment Links, Payment Element, ECE, in-app, Billing/Invoicing/Customer Portal/Radar/Connect, Checkout Sessions, Payment Intents with setup_future_usage, Setup Intents and off-session. It excludes PMME, Managed Payments and Terminal. These are broad product support flags, not proof every UI/API path has identical setup or merchant eligibility. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:145-169; old raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md:78-85; current wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay.md:29.

Amazon-hosted customer authorization precedes Stripe's immediate confirmation and redirect to merchant success page; return alone is not independent payment-success evidence. Amazon controls hosted step duration and Stripe does not configure that authorization-session timeout. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:170-182; old raw/stripe-amazon-pay-2025.md:12. The May accept-payment detail independently describes a 10-minute requires_action PaymentIntent window at raw/stripe-amazon-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:681-685, also summarized at wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay-accept-payment.md:13,21; scope and date these rather than treating them as a global contradiction or universal timeout.

New transaction ID is optional and lives on the Charge: expand PaymentIntent.latest_charge to access latest_charge.payment_method_details.amazon_pay.transaction_id, or retrieve that Charge; without expansion latest_charge is just a Charge ID. Stripe passes descriptor to Amazon, but Amazon/funding source control display. New raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:184-188.

Existing summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay.md:31 says full Connect with no restrictions and wiki/sources/source-stripe-amazon-pay.md:29 says no invite required for recurring; new raw/stripe-payments-amazon-pay-2026-11-07.md:20,63,162,167-169 shows broad platform and recurring support but does not expressly prove universal unrestricted availability or lack of invite. Keep the support facts and qualify unsupported account-level claims.

source_assessments.reason: The new capture adds material eligibility, dispute, support and reconciliation boundaries, and the existing source has a material claim-deadline overgeneralization.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/amazon-pay, the November capture documents a reusable Amazon Pay wallet: worldwide customers authenticate through Amazon using stored credentials, Stripe confirms after Amazon authorizes, and the customer returns to a merchant page. Eligible account locations are the same 17 listed in the older capture; 16 European locations can present 12 listed currencies, while US accounts use USD. It names a prohibited crypto MCC, 0.50 USD/GBP/EUR minima, recurring and manual/partial capture, 90-day refund submission, 240-day general dispute filing and a full product/API matrix. New raw lines 9-100 and 102-194 distinguish Amazon authorization, Stripe confirmation, Refund and Dispute statuses, PaymentIntent versus Charge, and optional Amazon transaction ID. Old raw lines 8-83 and 107-151 already supported much of the wallet, currency and dispute baseline. source-stripe-amazon-pay.md lines 13-35 captures those basics but lacks the new restriction, path support and claim-specific evidence deadline.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/amazon-pay, substantive November changes include explicit US USD-only currency mapping, MCC 6051 prohibition, separate chargeback versus A-to-z claim deadlines and fees, broader product/API support, Amazon-controlled hosted authorization timing, and optional Charge-based transaction ID retrieval (new raw lines 18-51, 102-188). Reorganized headings, removal of the old video, and links to child guides are presentation or navigation; they do not deprecate older path details. Old raw lines 107-142 retain the May refund wording, ten-day generic dispute text, and an internal US-currency table/prose conflict as dated evidence. source-stripe-amazon-pay.md needs reciprocal qualification: usually ten days for chargebacks, six for claims, actual due_by controlling; US USD only; broad support flags cannot prove unrestricted Connect or live off-session eligibility. The separate May integration’s ten-minute PaymentIntent requires_action window has a different subject from the November Amazon-hosted session statement, and a merchant return page alone does not prove a successful payment.
